pr_title: Reject font values that are invalid for pango
pr_body:
Use pango to parse font configuration early, and reject the command as
invalid if the value is invalid for pango. Since we're already parsing
the font into a `PangoFontDescription`, keep that instance around and
avoid re-parsing the font each time we render text.

Fixes: https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/6805
pr_comments:
This LGTM!

Follow-up issue: also pass a parsed `PangoFontDescription` to other text-related functions like `render_text`, but that's a more involved change.

I'd missed that one! That was quicker than expected (took less than my lunch in the oven :joy: ).

I wonder if `swaynag` and `swaybar` should fall back to `"monospace 10"` if the given input is invalid too. That's out of scope tho; the current versions will also misrender if the input font is invalid.

comments:
`git bisect` for this winds up on commit 62d90a8e959c6edcc752e124a9928cfa2399fbd1.

At least in my case, explicitly setting the font size with e.g. `font pango:mono bold 10` (as opposed to `font pango:mono bold`) alleviated the issue; this seems like an issue with poor defaults.

Yes, explicit font size fixed it. Probably restoring the fallback mechanism or prohibiting the syntax in config file lacking a size is a way to go. The former option has an advantage of being backward compatible though.

We've two options here:

- Reject `font pango:mono bold` as an invalid config (missing font size). Ignore the whole line and retain any previously existing font config.
- Accept `font pango:mono bold`. Use this font family, but fall back to a default size since a size is missing.

The former is probably simpler to implement and more resilient. Any preference, @emersion ?
Do we have a reliable way to check whether a pango font description is correct?

I believe that using `pango_font_description_from_string` should work:

> Any one of the options may be absent. If FAMILY-LIST is absent, then the family_name field of the resulting font description will be initialized to NULL. If STYLE-OPTIONS is missing, then all style options will be set to the default values. If SIZE is missing, the size in the resulting font description will be set to 0.

We can check that the `family != NULL && size != 0` and reject the value otherwise.

Additionally, we could keep this `PangoFontDescription*` instance around as an attribute of the config object, rather than create a new `PangoFontDescription*` instance each time we render a titlebar.
Ah, cool! It would be quite nice to reject invalid pago font descriptions as invalid config yes.
Those affected here: can you test #7092?

review_comments:
In this branch, I think it makes sense to do:

```c
config->font = font + 6;
free(font[0..5]); // Pseudocode, not sure how to free just the first 5 bytes.
```

This avoids one unecessary `strdup`. Does this make sense? If so, how would you
do this?

That's not possible.

But it doesn't matter too much anyways, we shouldn't try micro-optimizing too hard.

Can we call the `font` command here with arg `"monospace 10"`?

We'd be able to de-duplicate some font-configuration bits, and also drop the
extra call to `config_update_font_height` below (which is kind of a hack). In
fact, we can move the logic from `config_update_font_height` into the font
command itself, since the font height only changes when the font changes, and
drop the separate `config_update_font_height` entirely.

Does this seem reasonable?
I'd rather not execute commands when initializing data structures.
I'll re-think how to optimise that further and address it separately then. It's a non-issue in this scope.

This has a risk that the value will (for only an instant) be NULL, so if
another thread tries to read it, it'll fail. Could this be an issue? Should I
reassign _and then_ `free`?
No, it's fine, Sway is single-threaded.
